title: Even Semester B.E. Examinations - Data Structures
instructions: Revealing of Identity in any form in the answer book will be treated as malpractice.
Answer any five questions choosing one full question from each unit.

parts.text: Define a structure “Faculty” with the following fields: faculty name, department name, designation, year of service. Write a C program using this structure to read details of n faculty members and print details of those with >20 years experience and belonging to ISE department.
Explain with general syntax and example, the following file functions: fopen(), getc(), fprintf(), fseek().
Read n integers at the command line and store them in a file. Compute the sum and average of all the integers and store the result at the end of the same file.
Consider two files LIST1 and LIST2 containing integer elements. Write a C program to produce third file MERGE to concat two lists. Display the contents of all three files.
Write a C program to read two integer arrays and check whether they are identical or not using pointers.
Explain the methods by which the values of a structure can be transferred from one function to another along with advantages and disadvantages of each method.
Write C functions to perform operations on Stack: Push character onto Stack; Pop character from stack; Transfer contents of Stack1 to Stack2 maintaining element order.
How circular queue is different from a linear queue? Write a C program to implement circular queue of integers using static memory allocation.
Write a C program to compute sum of the series 1 + x + x² + x³ + … + xⁿ with the help of recursive functions.
Consider a producer-consumer problem: buffer of size n. Consumer consumes in order produced. Mention data structure and develop C program.
Develop a C recursive program to compute the sum of first n natural numbers.
Convert the following infix expressions to equivalent prefix and postfix expressions: (A+(B-C)*D)+E/F; P^(Q+R)–S/T*(U+W).
